item.title: ‘Not a close case:’ Judge blocks review of ABC’s broadcast licenses
item.description: A federal judge ruled that the Federal Communications Commission “may not retaliate against or punish Plaintiffs and other broadcast license holders for disfavored speech.”

media:content.media:title: The ruling is a blow for FCC Chair Brendan Carr's media agenda.

item.dc:creator: By John Hendel, Josh Gerstein and Kyle Cheney
item.dc:contributor: By John Hendel, Josh Gerstein and Kyle Cheney

item.title: FCC authorizes Elon Musk’s plans for data centers in space
item.description: Brendan Carr said the decision could usher in a million of the orbital centers and boost U.S. prominence in artificial intelligence.

media:content.media:title: Elon Musk said these space plans will help both the U.S. and world.

item.dc:creator: By John Hendel

item.title: House Dems demand clarity on Homeland Security tech contracts
item.description: Democrats have requested information from companies including Palantir, Flock and Clearview AI about how their technology is being used by the Department of Homeland Security.

media:content.media:title: A mobile surveillance camera stands near the Washington Monument in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 27, 2026. The Trump administration has deployed cameras near multiple construction projects on the National Mall and throughout the city citing concerns of vandalism.

item.dc:creator: By Gabby Miller

item.title: Nvidia braces for a long fight on Capitol Hill
item.description: Nvidia has assembled a cadre of Washington lawyers and lobbyists including congressional investigations attorney Joshua A. Levy ahead of Jensen Huang’s testimony next week.

item.title: Huang’s return rattles Sacramento and Silicon Valley
item.description: Nvidia’s CEO is back at the helm. California officials and industry insiders can’t agree whether that’s a triumph or a liability.

media:content.media:title: Nvidia’s board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and president.
